entries.07bd7371dae76cb5: This region is handled by Guangzhou Aleisiti Automotive Parts Co., Ltd. and Hefei Aleisiti Automotive Parts Co., Ltd. in China, and by Ahresty India Private Limited and others in India. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, external customer revenue was ¥36,228 million (down 0.8% year on year), and segment profit was ¥828 million (down 54.2% year on year). The securities report states that the reasons for lower profit were that, in China, order volumes declined due to lower sales at some major customers, and, in India, production of some products was unstable, which increased production costs. Aleisiti Precision Mold (Guangzhou) Co., Ltd., which had been included in this segment, transferred all of its equity interest in July 2025 and was removed from the scope of consolidation.

entries.147bd8d5764d3921: This is the business that manufactures and sells die-cast products (cast products made by pouring molten aluminum alloy into a mold under high pressure), mainly for automobiles, and it is the core of the group. The main products are die-cast products mainly for automobiles, mold-cast products and dies for die casting. It supplies products to customers through product design (including analysis of molten metal flow and strength), die manufacturing, prototyping and mass production (die casting, machining and so on), and almost all group companies take part in some stage of this series of processes. The annual securities report divides the reportable segments into 3 regions, because this business is developed with strategies set for each of Japan, North America and Asia. It states that since 9 tenths or more of the die-casting business's operating revenue comes from automobile-related business, its results are strongly affected by automobile production volumes in Japan and overseas.
entries.218f1d421f9aa57a: The region handled by AHRESTY WILMINGTON CORP. in Ohio, USA, and AHRESTY MEXICANA S.A. de C.V. in Mexico. Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥52,209 million (up 5.0% year on year), and order volumes increased owing to factors such as the start of mass production of new products. On the other hand, manufacturing costs such as labor costs at the US plant continued to rise, and the segment loss was ¥428 million (compared with a segment loss of ¥1,617 million in the previous fiscal year). The securities report makes improving the profitability of the US plant its top priority. AHRESTY WILMINGTON CORP. in the US is in a state of negative net worth, and the amount of negative net worth as of the end of March 2026 is noted as ¥1,075 million.

Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥6,622 million (down 8.2% year on year), and segment profit was ¥253 million (up 11.9% year on year). The report states that sales fell because the weight sold decreased 10.4% from the previous year, while profit rose because selling prices also tended to rise in response to higher purchase prices.

entries.76501878ac5abf1c: This is a business in which the group manufactures free-access floors (raised double floors for buildings) and similar products, and the company installs and sells them. AHRESTY Tochigi Co., Ltd. and Hefei Aleisiti Automotive Parts Co., Ltd. manufacture floor panels and other products. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, external customer revenue was ¥3,457 million (down 29.2% year on year), and segment profit was ¥437 million (down 45.1% year on year). The reason is given as a year-on-year decline in orders for large cleanroom projects at semiconductor-related companies, which are its main customers.
entries.7d2ea2e82d1528ab: The region handled by the Company and its domestic consolidated subsidiaries (AHRESTY Tochigi Corporation, AHRESTY Kumamoto Corporation, AHRESTY Yamagata Corporation, AHRESTY Techno Service Corporation, and AHRESTY Daimold Hamamatsu Corporation). Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥68,574 million (up 6.2% year on year), and segment profit was ¥2,638 million (up 13.7% year on year). The securities report gives the increase in orders accompanying the recovery in domestic automobile production, and the reduction in fixed costs from the right-sizing of headcount carried out in the previous fiscal year, as the reasons for the increases in sales and profit.
entries.843640bba4f33ebf: Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥167,092 million, an increase of ¥4,162 million (2.6%) from the previous year. The annual securities report cites as reasons an increase in order volumes from key customers following the recovery of domestic automobile production, and the start of mass production of new products. Domestic revenue was ¥78,653 million and overseas revenue was ¥88,438 million.

entries.a42e0ff2ff96c987: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥3,739 million (up 10.9% year on year), ordinary profit was ¥2,865 million (down 5.9%), and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥3,580 million (the previous year was a net loss of ¥2,892 million). The annual securities report states that operating profit and net income increased due to the effects of structural reforms, including the appropriate scaling of headcount implemented in the previous year, and the recovery in order volumes, and that the company returned to profit for the current period for the first time in seven periods. Ordinary profit decreased from the previous year due to a decrease in non-operating income and an increase in non-operating expenses. Meanwhile, the North American segment continued to record a loss, and the company has made improving the profitability of its U.S. plant its top priority. The annual securities report states that, due to soaring raw material and energy prices stemming from the situation in the Middle East, results for the next period are expected to fall below those of the current period.
